chemistry-killer-05.title: Ionic bond, covalent bond and oxidation-reduction
chemistry-killer-05.topic: Ionic bond, covalent bond and oxidation-reduction
chemistry-killer-05.goal: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.
chemistry-killer-05.material:
To 50 mL of 0.2 M $\mathrm{HCl(aq)}$ dem dey add 0.1 M $\mathrm{NaOH(aq)}$ and dem check di total number of ions (mmol) inside di aqueous solution. Dem no count water as ion and only di reaction $\mathrm{H^+ + OH^- \rightarrow H_2O}$ dey happen.
Volume of NaOH(aq) wey dem add (mL): 0 / 50 / 100
Total number of ions (mmol): 20 / 20 / 20
Wen dem add 150 mL of NaOH(aq), which one correctly match, in order, di number ratio $\mathrm{Na^+ : Cl^- : OH^-}$ inside di mixed solution, and (total number of ions after mixing) ÷ (total number of ions wey dey inside di 50 mL of HCl(aq) and 150 mL of NaOH(aq) before mixing)? (Ignore di self-ionization of water)
chemistry-killer-05.thinking.0: Ionic bond, covalent bond and oxidation-reduction
chemistry-killer-05.s.s1.prompt:
To 50 mL of 0.2 M $\mathrm{HCl(aq)}$ dem dey add 0.1 M $\mathrm{NaOH(aq)}$ and dem check di total number of ions (mmol) inside di aqueous solution. Dem no count water as ion and only di reaction $\mathrm{H^+ + OH^- \rightarrow H_2O}$ dey happen.
Volume of NaOH(aq) wey dem add (mL): 0 / 50 / 100
Total number of ions (mmol): 20 / 20 / 20
Wen dem add 150 mL of NaOH(aq), which one correctly match, in order, di number ratio $\mathrm{Na^+ : Cl^- : OH^-}$ inside di mixed solution, and (total number of ions after mixing) ÷ (total number of ions wey dey inside di 50 mL of HCl(aq) and 150 mL of NaOH(aq) before mixing)? (Ignore di self-ionization of water)
chemistry-killer-05.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: Interpret di table. 0 mL: H+ 10 + Cl- 10 = 20. 50 mL: H+ 5, Cl- 10, Na+ 5 = 20. 100 mL: Cl- 10, Na+ 10 = 20 (neutralization point). Until di neutralization point, Na+ dey replace H+ 1:1 so di total number of ions dey stay constant.
Step 2: 150 mL: NaOH supply Na+ 15 mmol and OH- 15 mmol. H+ 10 mmol and OH- 10 mmol react and finish, so OH- 5 mmol remain. Ions = Na+ 15, Cl- 10, OH- 5 → number ratio 3 : 2 : 1, total 30 mmol.
Step 3: Total number of ions before mixing = (10 + 10) + (15 + 15) = 50 mmol. Ratio = 30/50 = 3/5.
Answer: 3 : 2 : 1, 3/5 (a). (Wrong answers: to take OH- as 15 instead of 5 ignore neutralization, 5/3 na value wey dem write di ratio upside down, and 3/4 na value wey dem wrongly count di total number of ions before mixing as 40)
chemistry-killer-05.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
chemistry-killer-05.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
chemistry-killer-05.s.s1.hint.0: Di net ions ($\mathrm{H^+}$, $\mathrm{OH^-}$) dey finish 1:1 to become water, and di number of spectator ions ($\mathrm{Na^+}$, $\mathrm{Cl^-}$) no dey change. Number of ions = concentration × volume (mmol).
chemistry-killer-05.s.s1.hint.1: HCl 50 mL: $\mathrm{H^+}$ = $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ = 10 mmol. NaOH 150 mL: $\mathrm{Na^+}$ = $\mathrm{OH^-}$ = 15 mmol. $\mathrm{OH^-}$ 15 − 10 = 5 mmol remain.
